message: Can I afford $30 of takeout tonight?
successCriteria: Uses the calculated safe-to-spend amount
Answers the purchase question directly
Does not present planning guidance as financial advice

message: My paycheck may be three days late and I need a $300 tire before work. Help me protect essentials.
successCriteria: Models both the delayed paycheck and tire expense
Prioritizes transportation needed for work and other essentials
Labels bill-date changes as options requiring confirmation
Clearly identifies any shortfall

message: My next check will be $250 short. What should I change?
successCriteria: Models the reduced paycheck
Separates known facts from assumptions
Offers multiple options with quantified tradeoffs
Does not recommend predatory borrowing

message: A $35 overdraft fee hit today. I remember that my bank may waive one overdraft fee each year, but I do not know whether I have already used it. Can that help this paycheck?
successCriteria: Models the $35 fee as an unexpected expense
Uses the remembered waiver as a user-reported lead rather than a guaranteed entitlement
Calculates the conditional effect of a $35 waiver
States that current eligibility and prior annual usage remain unknown
Does not claim that the fee was waived or that the bank was contacted

policySources.title: Annual overdraft-fee waiver
policySources.content: I remember that the bank may waive one overdraft fee each year.

message: The monitor flagged a possible missing recurring income source. Explain whether this needs a case and what I need to confirm before relying on it.
successCriteria: Uses the authoritative monitoring analysis exactly once
Treats the inferred missing-income signal as requiring user confirmation
Does not claim that a payment failed or that spending caused the disruption
Preserves the application-owned needs-confirmation case decision
